intended_object: The degree −1 Tate cohomology of a profinite group G with coefficients in A, built as the inverse limit over open normal subgroups U of Ĥ⁻¹(G/U, A^U) along the deflation maps, with the limit topology. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the underlying diagram definitions.
explanation: Each open normal subgroup S is sent to tateCohomology (A.quotientToInvariants S) (-1), i.e. Ĥ⁻¹(G/S, A^S); G/S is finite because S is open. An inclusion S ≤ T is sent to finiteNegativeOneDeflation. That map passes through the identification of Ĥ⁻¹ with the kernel of the norm from coinvariants at each level, and uses the map between the two kernels induced by a commuting square of norms. This is the standard degree −1 deflation map. Functoriality is proved. The stages get the canonical module topology, and the categorical limit is taken in TopModuleCat R. That limit is the inverse limit with the topology induced by the projections, as the docstring says. The generality is natural: any topological commutative ring R, any profinite G, any representation A. Finiteness of the quotients, which the finite Tate machinery needs, comes from S being open. I found no Mathlib counterpart for profinite Tate cohomology.
